steps.text: You hear? The Mountbelan girl's back in old Victoria, smack dab in the middle of Caladon.
Here? I thought she'd be off in a bigger city. There's no place more infected than this, and didn't it have a bout of Reunion or something too? I thought she couldn't stand all that?
She's working for the council.
Ahh—the council. The venerable city council. She probably has it easy as could be.
Is that all you're interested in? I thought you'd be delighted.
Delighted? About what?
Haven't you been wanting a leg up for that factory of yours? We all know she's got her head up her behind, and you know what she's done before. She hates the Infected to death.
So now she's working for the council. You find her, let her know what's in it for her, tell her about your factory, and there you go—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: ...What is this? An invitation?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: 'We cordially invite you on this day... to share in our celebrations. Champagne tasting and tours... tonight at 8 P.M. We hope to see you there.'

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: A class reunion? Sometimes it really does puzzle me how something both so time-wasting, and so difficult to refuse, ever got folded into 'etiquette.'

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I'll go once hours are over. I just hope the rotten lot of them don't give me any—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Mmph. No, bad. No need for anger on the job.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Let's just get ourselves straight to work.

steps.name: Haughty Noble Alumnus
steps.text: Oh, hello, old friend. Just last week we met at the drinking party. Your magnificent visage stole the breath from quite a number of people! They've been clamoring to have you back again!

steps.name: Self-Satisfied Noble Alumna
steps.text: My face, is it?

steps.name: Self-Satisfied Noble Alumna
steps.text: They're just after my estate. I'm not sure I can blame them; it turned me what would normally be a year's profits in a few short months.

steps.name: Self-Satisfied Noble Alumna
steps.text: Aren't people still praising Count Adam's dashing appearance, even though his hair resembles corn silk more than anything by now?

steps.name: Haughty Noble Alumnus
steps.text: *cough*! You haven't changed a whit.

steps.name: Haughty Noble Alumnus
steps.text: Now, profits, though, you'll want to hear about my winery. I think you'll find that's the real last say...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: (Jockeying with each other, flaunting assets, backstabbing the absent. Hmph. These people don't change one jot.)

steps.name: Opportunistic Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Count Ambulas, my factory has been set on the right track, and I owe it to your kind attention! But before it can tithe you further profits, I will need just the tiniest sum more...

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah-hah-hah, it's a true honor you should still remember me! I was sat right behind you, if you remember!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: If you'd be willing to cast an eye over my estate, I'd be greatly thankful! ...Ah, I see. Sorry to bother you...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: (Treating a dinner party as a springboard up... these people do love their flattery. Honestly... what a typical sight.)

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: (I've been here for long enough—it's time I left. It'll take a while to get back to Caladon too.)

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, it really is you!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: You must try some of the champagne tonight, I'll bring you a glass...

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Of all the places to meet you! Do you still remember me? I was sat right behind you in class. I see you've found yourself a fine job!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Excuse me. If it's nothing urgent, I have my own business to attend to.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah, well, here's the thing, I hear you're working for the council now, and I just so happen to run a little factory. It's nothing too grand, but...

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: With just the right opportunity, it could turn a profit on par with Isabella's estate! And naturally I'd give you—my good official—a fabulous token of my thanks.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: So, for example, anything council-related...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I have absolutely no interest.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: (Could it... be this girl has no clue what my factory even does?)

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: (She's not one bit less sheltered. Nobles... snooty bloodline-obsessed elitists, the lot of them... Am I not being deferential enough for you—?!)

spans.text: (She's not one bit less sheltered. Nobles... snooty bloodline-obsessed elitists, the lot of them... Am I not being

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, my factory is right here in Caladon, if you didn't know. And it's only even here thanks to the great pains I know you and the councilors have gone to.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Haven't you always hated those lowly brutes? I know they paid quite the rightful price for what they did to your beloved pet.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: But now—thanks to these policies—the council has finally turned its head our way, hasn't it? Those lowly people exist for our sakes, and I've picked up by now on how to make good and proper use of them—

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: If I could just grasp one inch further, I'm sure results would be even more plentiful. And you, Miss Mountbelan, would have me doing all I could to repay your kindness!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: (How about I burn him to—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: No. No.)

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: You know, I'm finding it a little oddly hot in here.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, what do you say? How about we step outside and chat?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: (Can I really not just—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: No, no. I can't.)

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Here's my business card. Please, by all means!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: ...Hrmmph. Let me see.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: 'Barum's Works'?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Exactly!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I see. Well, Barum's Works.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Have you heard of it?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: We've discussed plans for new acts where your factory has served as a case study.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: My professor and I kept tabs on your factory in private too. 'Barum's Works' was top of the list that came in.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah, really! Now that's an honor! Then may I...?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I've already signed a non-disclosure agreement.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Of course! Naturally you wouldn't be the sort to break confidentiality! I was just hoping you could let me in on a little of the council chatter, some teatime topics, maybe we could chew the cud on this or that.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Such as...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Such as the act we're imminently proposing regarding working hours?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Exactly!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: If I could invite you to my factory for a look around, I'd be utterly honored...

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, you have my gratitude for deigning to come here. I had them clean the place thorough a few days ago. Not a speck of dust left!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Didn't I tell you I was here to see things as they are?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Oh, well, cleaning up some dust off to the side wouldn't impact your understanding of how our factory operates.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: I don't mean to boast, but you see, the scale of this place—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Not top of the line for Caladon, but remarkable all the same.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I see facilities and protective measures are kept in good order. In the light of present regulations, your site is a clean pass.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Security measures are also fully replete as stipulated.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, I see you've been underestimating me. It's only natural such fundamental work is well done.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: How about we take a look at the workshop? It's Infected, however, so even with protective measures ready, I'm sure you wouldn't want to go insi—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I would.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah, I see, it's that kerfuffle from a few years ago. You want to see if there's any traces of that whole... Reunion Movement inside?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Mm, yes, Reunion.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: My workers here have all gone through background checks, but you can rest assured, if you're displeased to see anyone in there, you can be sure I'll—

spans.text: My workers here have all gone through background checks, but you can rest assured, if you're displeased to see
in there, you can be sure I'll—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I'll have to see for myself.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Yes, I understand, you'd better get your protective gear on, then. I'll just have to brave the elements...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Is this the place? Where are the workers?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, I didn't think you'd be so concerned with a place like this. How could I possibly have you mingling with Infected? I've ordered them all out for the time being, and the purifier installations are on at maximum.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Let's not stay in here for too long. I'll be honest, this is my first time in here too... er, in a while, I mean.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Ah. I'm just taking a look around.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: After all, by your accounts, this place has made you a pretty penny, so my interest is natural. Moreover, did you forget? I and my professor have been keeping a watch on your factory for some time now.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Yes, and I'm honored for it.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Infected are both convenient and less demanding in the way of assurances. I have to thank the council for providing such a fine workforce.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: What are those?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah, surveillance devices.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: We both know, you see, how people tend to skive without motivation or supervision.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: And these riot shields?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ahh. Even less of a concern. Infected don't take simply to discipline, nor are they content with what they have. I imagine you know better than I do. Without a method or two at hand, they'd never stay placid.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Aren't you concerned that just leaving your riot control gear here might cause fear in the Infected, even elicit disorder?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Well... hah-hah, you worry too much, Miss Mountbelan.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: They don't see it.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: They don't what...?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: —Miss Mountbelan, we've been in here for a while now. Should we step out? Even with all the precautions, there's always an off-chance.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Let's take the lift out and pull that gear off, and take some deep breaths. Nice, deep breaths!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan, old friend, there's no one but you and me in this lift, so let me be a little honest with you. This may just interest you more in my factory?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Don't be too disappointed with what you've seen. Putting all that aside, you've noticed, haven't you?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: The surveillance and riot control staff, and the armed installations. You can't make all your money in the open, you know that.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: What's down below us is the real deal.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: But it's too filthy underground. You won't need to cast your own eye.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Mm. I am very—satisfied with what you've just told me.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: It's very interesting.
Once again, the alumnus feels the temperature rise a notch.
He ascribes this to Skyfire's excitement at the opportunity. To make money, to continue trampling over the disgorged masses.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Even beasts in the wild know they should only pounce when they see prey. If I didn't show you the genuine article, I worry you'd be left cold.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Factories are a garden variety thing. I need something new in the works too, you know?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Ha! So I see.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Hah-hah-hah-hah, well, come, Miss Mountbelan. I've had this fine tipple stashed for years. Let's toast!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: To your sponsoring a factory of much potential, and my soon-to-be debut upon a bigger stage!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Hahaha.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Cheers.
Skyfire's temperature rises, starting from underfoot.
In just a blink, a fraction of a second, she could burn this whole factory to nothing, and save all the people trapped below.
But in another blink, she suppresses the smoldering rage in her head.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Professor, did you need me?

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: 'Infected rioters identifying as 'Reunion' gravely hurt by organization known as 'King's Wand.'' That's what the news is reporting.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Professor, they killed Phil!

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: And how you resolved the issue was hardly the only way to do so.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: If you let an eye for an eye blind you, Miss Mountbelan, then that is altogether contrary to how I've taught you.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: Have you forgotten what I first told you?

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: The issue of the Reunion Movement is not solely a matter of the Infected. If you wish to continue the way you're going, then go to the place I recommended you. Deepen your studies. See the outside, and I mean that.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: Don't disappoint me, Miss Mountbelan. You're a student of plentiful notions. Don't let your own emotions stifle you. Look past them.
Flames can burn anything you want to cinders, but they can't solve problems.
Stood there in the factory, she pinches the wine glass and settles her somewhat unsteady breathing.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I imagine you know when the next council meeting is.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Look forward to the good news.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Hah, hahahah, thank you, Miss Mountbelan!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Here's the long and short of it, Professor.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Barum's Works. One of the factories on the list when we put together the investigation into Infected rights.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I'd consulted you on it, whereupon we decided to send a spy to sniff around in secret. I've assembled a file on the inner workings of his factory.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: On top of which, I find out just a few days ago that this factory's owner was one of my very own classmates.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I initially wanted to send the whole thing up in flames—of course, I knew that was utterly wrong, and it wouldn't solve a single thing, just pile meaningless hassle on instead.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: But I revile, HATE, what he did. Seeking me out at a dinner function hoping for a backdoor into the council, brazenly spilling all about his factory's machinations right in front of a Member—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: His doing so is evidence that dozens upon dozens before him did the same, that countless people took to the same methods for their own underhanded gains.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Professor, it's obviously afoul of current regulations. But they've tried it, and they've found out they don't get punished, they just reap the benefits. That's what got them all to start doing it.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Truth be told, I do remember him, and I know that 'sat behind me' spiel he gave was true in my case.

spans.text: Truth be told, I do remember him, and I know that 'sat behind me' spiel he gave was

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: He said the same thing to every noble there, but he did sit in the seat right behind me.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: He used to... not be like this.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: He used to be—a good egg?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Not particularly, but he was hardly what he is now... I just wonder, was this all in his nature? I don't feel like it was, Professor.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: He just... tried slipping through a regulatory loophole, and found nobody even cared. And he just kept inching on and on until he got to this state.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: Are you—very conflicted right now, Miss Mountbelan?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: No, Professor, I'm not conflicted at all. I just feel a little...

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I'm not sure how to put it. But I know crystal clear what I ought to do.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Anne-Moses, if you could further debrief the Professor on this unscrupulous factory.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: Yes, Miss Mountbelan.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: I went into hiding near the factory per the intel Miss Mountbelan provided. My comms signal suffered severe interference whenever I approached its basement levels.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: I speculate an internal comms shield is installed. The Infected workers within are completely cut off from the outside world.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: Based on my observations over several days, deceased Infected have even been ported out in secret, and sent for disposal.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: And armed personnel inside are dedicated to guarding the underground factory and its facilities. The Infected workers above have no inkling of what's going on. They simply assume it must be vital products or something being watched.

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: Based on the data provided by Miss Mountbelan, I surmise it's the previously missing groups of acutely ill Infected workers inside—

steps.name: Informant
steps.text: Being acutely ill makes treatment unnecessary, so they're used as disposable labor, shut in the factory underground to work to their deaths. Then the factory tosses them out, and replenishes with a new batch of Infected workers.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: Hm... I see the picture now.

steps.name: Councilor Angst
steps.text: So, Miss Mountbelan, your method for dealing with this?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: My report concludes here.

steps.name: Councilors
steps.text: Mm, and why did we have to sit here for over ten minutes listening to you talk about this one piffling factory?

steps.name: Councilors
steps.text: This has little bearing on us. I hope you realize that.

steps.name: Councilors
steps.text: Did Councilor Angst really bring you here just to yank this little factory by the collar?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: What I wish to point out to you all is that the core of this incident is the missing Infected workers locked away here under armed surveillance, the curtailing of personal freedoms, even the covert disposal of the dead.

spans.text: What I wish to point out to you all is that the core of this incident is the missing Infected workers locked away here under armed surveillance, the curtailing of personal freedoms, even the covert disposal of the

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Adding to which, they work in environments of excessive Originium particulate concentration, without corresponding protective measures or communications equipment. Every point here is in violation of currently enacted policy.

spans.text: Adding to which, they work in environments of excessive Originium particulate concentration,
corresponding protective measures or communications equipment. Every point here is in violation of currently enacted policy.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Said enacted policy has led Caladon to be considered relatively relaxed on the Infected, hence why it could even draw such numbers of them to work here. It's the root of the city's development.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Should this incident leak, Caladon's external image will be in smithereens, and no more Infected will think to come here for work, full stop.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: All present, I trust this scenario would not be to your delight.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Thus, this will amount to no proposal, but simply a factory... cleanup. And for Caladon's reputation, the proper proceedings will be needed for a rescue of the Infected workers in the council's name.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: This seizure, too, must be in the council's name, for all the wider world to see.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: As for the perspectives of all present—

steps.name: Councilors
steps.text: We'll take a vote.

steps.name: Councilors
steps.text: Everyone, your views?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Wh—What the—?! Who are you?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: What are you coming in here for?!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Ah, er, it's all Infected in here, you see...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: You lot, downstairs.

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Downstairs? But downstairs is—

steps.name: Victorian Soldier A
steps.text: Sir! Large number of unlawfully armed personnel discovered!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier B
steps.text: Sir! Unlawful communications shielding terminal discovered and dismantled!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier A
steps.text: Large quantity of Infected found underground!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier B
steps.text: Basement levels have been identified as an illegal factory!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Mm. Situation verified.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Per council regulations, we are hereby shutting this location down as the law compels.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: And you—as stipulated by law—may not engage in any similar business for a five-year period.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: —Evacuate the Infected!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: Miss Mountbelan!!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Ah, it's you... what is it?

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: You—My factory?!

steps.name: Wheedling Merchant Alumnus
steps.text: I had people turn up at my factory out of nowhere this morning, and even the underground to boot, they—what the hell happened?!

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Oh! You mean the factory seizure.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Didn't you ask me for help before?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: There you go. I've helped you.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: You caught word about me, yes, but you didn't catch on.

spans.text: You caught word about me, yes, but you didn't

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I'm not just a Member of the Council, I'm also a Rhodes Island Operator. If you're not familiar, perhaps I can illuminate you—

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: I work to resolve issues for the Infected.

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: And more importantly, I work to seek their rights for them.
